name: container_contents
summary: Show the slots of any one thing and what is in them, nested: a locker, crate, machine, suit, backpack, or 'player' for the player's whole inventory. Read only.

help.text: Works on or off a data network. position and distance_m are where the thing is: for a thing in a slot, its outermost holder's (a stored item keeps no position of its own). Slot indexes here are what move_item takes. prefab_contains and name_contains keep the slots holding a match at any depth (empty slots go). To shape it: fields ["slots.index", "slots.occupant.prefab_name", "slots.occupant.quantity"], or a path read from each slot such as occupant.slots.occupant.prefab_name for what a backpack holds; omit ["slots.occupant.slots"] drops the inner slots.
help.keys: reference_id, prefab_name, display_name, position {x, y, z}, distance_m, slots [{index, name, slot_class, empty, occupant}], silo {count, capacity, entries_known, importing, exporting, dispense_slot, total, offset, entries}.

silo.text: On an SDB Silo the reply adds silo: {count and capacity in entries, entries_known (false on a multiplayer client, where only the host keeps the store), importing, exporting, dispense_slot (an IC's DispenseSlot, -1 for none), total, offset, entries [{index (0 is exported next), reference_id (always null), prefab_name, display_name, quantity, max_quantity, children, contents [{prefab_name, quantity}], rots_when_taken}]}. prefab_contains and name_contains filter the entries too. entries_limit and entries_offset page them.

reference_id.description: Any thing's reference id, or 'player' for the player.

depth.description: Levels of nested slots to show; default 3.

prefab_contains.description: Only slots holding this prefab name part at any depth.

entries_limit.description: A silo's stored entries to list; default 10.

entries_offset.description: A silo's stored entries to skip.
